recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit a formal pattern only if PA later introduces additional Patient-like resources or creates a new final decision requiring one.
issue_request: FHIR-14441 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification for R5 by PA. It asked whether to define a formal Patient-like pattern, but the approved resolution only required concrete alignment changes: Person.active after identifier, Person.identifier and Person.address in summary, Person.photo 0..*, and Practitioner telecom/gender/birthDate/address ordered like Patient; PA did not want a formal pattern unless future resources made one valuable.
initial_application: The issue was applied through related source history: commit 1410ca6ac9b4 changed Person.photo to 0..* under FHIR-20590, commit 1bf9c6c3a619 added Patient-like Person elements under FHIR-20771, and direct commit 7aa395b0f558 for FHIR-14441 added Person.identifier/address summary flags plus Practitioner/Person ordering and status cleanup.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively builds Patient, Person, Practitioner, and RelatedPerson. Current source keeps the common Patient-like order and flags; RelatedPerson's resource-specific patient/relationship/role elements do not conflict with FHIR-14441. PA January 2019 Confluence minutes repeat the tracker and note that it did not change Patient, and community issue-key searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence records.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current authoritative StructureDefinition source already has the approved Person and Practitioner alignments and because adding a formal pattern would contradict the Jira resolution.
